subject: The wardroom of the colony ship ariadne at supper, one table and one pot. Hamond has been in the galley since morning and has let nobody in. He comes out with a loaf, a real one, risen and brown, and sets it in the middle of the table like a baby. Then he stands and says a grace over it that takes in the flour, his mother and a promise that every supper from here to landfall will have one. Only these two officers are seen clearly; the other four at the table or on the ship are faceless: backs turned, in shadow or cut off by the frame.
